title: fix(plugin-auth): write the session last_activity_at heartbeat on every deployment
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoRcazFf3zbHR5zgBPMo64bA)_

Fixes #25343

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

The second and last half of #25343. The column half (`user_agent` and `last_activity_at` on the Sessions list views) landed as #25368. This half makes `last_activity_at` actually get written on a default deployment, so the Last Activity column is filled.

Ruling: 6358844136, letter A (maintainer 「同意」, 2026-10-23), per analysis 6357589247.

## What changes

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-password-session-policy.ts`, `enforceSessionControls` (run per authenticated request from `customSession`):

- **The heartbeat runs on every deployment.** The early return when the idle and absolute limits are both off (the default) is gone, and the `last_activity_at` write is no longer inside `if (idleMin > 0)`. It is still at most one write per session per minute (`SESSION_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS`, 60 s, the same threshold as before).
- **With both limits off, the read is throttled too.** A per-process, per-session memo (`SessionHeartbeatMemo`) remembers when each session's `sys_session` row was last read and skips the `findOne` (and so the write) for 60 s after it. The memo is bounded at `SESSION_HEARTBEAT_MEMO_MAX` (10,000) sessions, least recently read evicted first; an evicted session is simply read once more. It is held in a `WeakMap` keyed by the data engine, so in a running process it is the one engine's memo, and a second engine (another manager, a test double) never answers from it.
- **With a limit on, nothing about enforcement changes.** The memo is not consulted, so every request still reads the row, exactly as revocation needs. The heartbeat now also runs when only the absolute limit is configured (before, that configuration wrote no heartbeat either).
- A failed read is not memoised, so the next request reads again. When both limits are off, the read-failure warning now names what was lost (the heartbeat) instead of saying the idle and absolute limits were not evaluated, which on that deployment would name controls nobody turned on. With a limit on, the message is unchanged.
- The write-failure path (`logDurabilityDegradation` on the heartbeat update) is unchanged: same text, same meta, only re-indented one level.

`auth-manager.ts`: the `enforceSessionControls` docblock no longer says "No-op when both are off" (comment only).

## Measured cost

Under the default config, per live session per minute:

- **One request** reads `sys_session` once and, when `last_activity_at` is older than a minute, writes it once. Every other request in that minute reads nothing extra (the memo).
- **That same request resolves the caller's grants twice.** Core's request-grants memo (`packages/core/src/security/request-grants-memo.ts`) declines when a write lands inside the request, and the heartbeat is such a write. Measured in `session-grants-resolved-once.test.ts` for an organization member: the declined request reads 6 more grant rows than a memo-served one (`twice.reads.length - once.reads.length`, the existing pin). So the price is about 6 extra grant reads per session per minute, on top of the one read and one write.
- ADR-0127 D8 is confirmed on `main` (`docs/adr/0127-*.md` around :125): `sys_session` is deliberately outside the grants cache's watched set, so the heartbeat does not retire the authorization cache. The cost above is the per-request memo, not the cache.

## Verification

- New `session-heartbeat-default-config.test.ts`, 11 cases: heartbeat written under the default config (first request, and again after more than 60 s); the memo skips the read and the write within 60 s and reads again at 60 s + 1 ms; a row touched by another process 20 s ago is read but not written; per session; per engine; a failed read is not memoised and its warning names the heartbeat; a revoked session is read once a minute and never touched; the memo cap evicts the least recently read; with an idle timeout or an absolute max on, two requests a second apart both read.
- `auth-manager.test.ts`: the pin "is a no-op when idle + absolute are both off" asserted that `findOne` is never called, which is the behaviour the ruling reverses. It is rewritten in place to "revokes nothing but still writes the heartbeat". The idle-timeout and absolute-max pins beside it are unchanged and green.
- `session-grants-resolved-once.test.ts`: its warm-up asserted that the warm request writes nothing. A session's first request now writes the heartbeat, so the warm-up makes one request per session and expects exactly `update sys_session` from each; the measured requests after it write nothing, as before, and every count in the file is unchanged. The pin "a write inside the request: the memo declines" gains a default-config row beside its idle-timeout row.
- Ablation: `idleMin > 0 &&` put back in front of the heartbeat condition (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 to 0, blob `b6da2ab9` to `8519f0aa`; the tests import `src/`, no `dist/` on the path). 15 cases went red, including both "heartbeat written under the default config" pins, the rewritten no-op pin and the default-config grants-memo row. Restored: blob back to `b6da2ab9`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test`: 188 files, 3538 passed, 10 skipped (at `302d5e29`; the two commits after it change only `session-heartbeat-default-config.test.ts` and the ledger below, and the three touched suites re-ran at `af4a5fe5`: 326/326). `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` (tsc, examples, `check:test-typecheck`) exit 0 at `af4a5fe5`; the test-typecheck debt ledger is unchanged.
- The new suite's engine double opens `findOne` / `update` with `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` / `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`, and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains its two rows (`check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write`, 0 lost).
- Gates at `af4a5fe5`: `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 79; `--ran` with recorded exit codes: 79 accounted, 78 run, 1 NOT MEASURED (`node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` exits 3, it needs an unshallowed clone). `pnpm check:dts-closure` and `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 1 on a local `packages/plugins/organizations/dist` with no `index.d.ts` (a package this diff does not touch); after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/organizations build --force` both exit 0. `pnpm check:durability-log-level` and `pnpm check:engine-double-contract` exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- The heartbeat's write-failure message still explains its consequence in idle-timeout terms ("this session will be revoked as idle EARLIER"). On a deployment with no idle timeout the real consequence is only a stale Last Activity. The dispatch asked for that path to stay exactly as it is, so it is unchanged here.
- The memo is per process, as ruled. On a multi-node deployment a session served by several nodes can be read once a minute per node; the write is still guarded by the row's own `last_activity_at`.
- The raw `user_agent` shown as browser and OS is the objectui polish item noted on the card, not part of this PR.
